name: Dar es Salaam

newFindings.source: Tanzania Ministry of Lands, Survey and Mapping Department
newFindings.evidence: Official mandate covers cadastral/topographic/geodetic surveys, converting survey data into charts/maps/plans, and maintaining national mapping infrastructure. The page describes departmental functions, not an open parcel API.

newFindings.source: Tanzania Ministry of Lands, Huduma ya Upimaji na Ramani brochure
newFindings.evidence: Official service brochure describes map products, including electronic maps for some urban/municipal areas, as products supplied on application/for a fee. Cadastral-map and plan-registration services are agency workflows, not evidence of unrestricted bulk access.

newFindings.source: Dar es Salaam 20,000 plot survey project
newFindings.evidence: Official project document describes a plot surveying/allocation process in Dar; it does not publish a reusable parcel feature layer.
Previously reviewed official land-services application uses an account-oriented workflow. No anonymous parcel query/download endpoint was identified.

Public geospatial portal inventory reviewed in the prior pass showed thematic/admin layers (e.g. schools, reserves, hazards), not cadastral plots. The portal host/operator status was not independently established as an authoritative cadastral publisher.

newFindings.source: ArcGIS Online public catalog search, exact Dar parcel query
newFindings.evidence: Returned one feature service, Dar Es Salaam Damage Assessment. Direct service metadata identifies point layers for commercial/residential buildings and public facilities and describes a structural-damage collection, so this is a project/assessment service, not cadastral polygons.

newFindings.source: ArcGIS Online public catalog item TZ Lands_WFL1
newFindings.evidence: A fresh exact ArcGIS search returned a Feature Service with one polygon layer called Parcel (17 features). A bounded 1-feature query returned a polygon and the metadata advertises ParcelNo as an identifier field. Its small extent is [39.11553,-6.59489,39.12617,-6.58302], approximately 29 km northwest of the WUP city point; count within 1 km of that point is zero. This is a genuine public nearby parcel candidate, but source authority and Dar-wide coverage are unverified.

sourceQuality: The ArcGIS Damage Assessment service is non-cadastral based on its own description and point geometry. TZ Lands_WFL1 is a public third-party ArcGIS-hosted polygon layer named Parcel, with a nonempty ParcelNo field and one sampled polygon, but its item only says “Tanzania land bank.” No source authority or Dar municipal affiliation is documented; its extent is 28.7 km from the target point.
blocker: A public partial parcel candidate exists, but its extent lies about 28.7 km from the WUP point, a 1 km centre count is zero, and the item does not document Dar-city affiliation. No city-centre parcel geometry or authoritative registry endpoint was found.
remainingUncertainty: The partial polygon layer may refer to land in the wider Dar region, but no municipal boundary overlay or authoritative source attribution was established. Do not generalize its 17 features citywide or treat its nonempty ParcelNo as a city match.
nextStep: Ask the publishing agency or data custodian for the service scope/authority and a published endpoint whose extent includes the WUP point or documented Dar municipality; then make a bounded parcel-ID+geometry query.
